unknown_mechanisms.name: binding and unified conscious access
unknown_mechanisms.current_claim_boundary: Brain may implement workspace-style coordination and reportable access proxies, but it must preserve the open status of phenomenal consciousness and neural binding.
allowed_uses: route competing signals through attention and working-memory control
preserve separate reportable-access and subjective-experience labels
force HOLD on claims that require consciousness equivalence
research_questions: which access-control mechanisms improve task performance without overclaiming consciousness
which internal reports are useful while remaining non-phenomenal proxies

unknown_mechanisms.name: emotion to value mapping
unknown_mechanisms.current_claim_boundary: Brain may map affect-like signals to value, salience and avoidance heuristics, but it must not claim literal human emotion replication.
forbidden_claims: reward and pain scores equal biological affect
allowed_uses: score urgency, risk, loss and reinforcement
flag high-pressure states for operator review
separate functional valence from felt experience
research_questions: which affect-like signals improve economic and cognitive decisions
where should pain/reward signals be blocked from governance mutation

unknown_mechanisms.name: self-model continuity and identity
unknown_mechanisms.current_claim_boundary: Brain may maintain persistent identity, goals, policies and autobiographical records, but it must not claim human selfhood or personhood.
forbidden_claims: persistent state equals a human self
allowed_uses: track autobiographical state as operational memory
research_questions: which self-model fields improve planning and safety
which identity changes require human approval
